options: Verifying the correctness and quality of data against its source
Reducing the number of rows pulled from a table
Assigning monetary value to data assets
questions.explanation: Data Validation verifies the correctness and quality of data against the source; in other words, it reconciles imported and processed data with the source data.

questions.stem: By when must Data Validation be completed at the latest?
options: Before data is pulled from the source
Before the database is backed up
Before data is passed to end users
questions.explanation: Validation can be done before pulling data and after processing it, but it must be done before data is passed to end users.

questions.stem: When data changes its shape during transformation from source to target, what is Data Validation conducted against?
options: The business rules implemented during transformation
A synthetic copy of the data
questions.explanation: Where transformation changes the shape of the data, validation is performed against the business rules applied during that transformation.

options: The structure of tables and columns
Primary keys, foreign keys, unique, not null, value checks and query performance constraints
Whether column data types match their contents
questions.explanation: Constraints Validation checks the accuracy of all types of constraints, including primary and foreign keys, unique, not null, value checks and query performance constraints.

questions.stem: Which type of Data Validation checks the structure of tables and columns?
questions.explanation: Structured Validation is the check on the structures of tables and columns.

questions.stem: Which example illustrates Data Range Validation?
options: Ensuring a Date column only accepts date-formatted values
Checking that foreign keys resolve to a parent row
Ensuring that only the latest data is processed when only latest data is allowed
Checking that code follows optimised patterns
Confirming a table has the expected columns
questions.explanation: Data Range Validation checks the allowable range for processing, for instance that only the latest data is processed when that is the rule.

options: The primary key of every table
The number of rows in each table
Whether values fall within a date range
The quality of the syntax and whether code is written in an optimised way
questions.explanation: Code Validation checks the quality of the syntax, recognising that there are ways to write quality, optimised code.

questions.stem: If a column's data type is Date, which validation ensures only date-formatted values are processed?
questions.explanation: Data Type Validation checks the type of data to be processed, so a Date column should only receive values in date format.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the listed types of Data Validation?
questions.explanation: The five listed types are Constraints, Structured, Data Range, Code and Data Type Validation; Encryption Validation is not among them.

questions.stem: Data Validation can be described as reconciliation between which two things?
options: The data catalogue and the data inventory
Imported and processed data, and its source data
questions.explanation: Validation is the reconciliation of imported and processed data with the source data from which it came.
